subject: Fallthrough behavior and rate-limit qualification — next tests
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Walker <sarah.walker@aegishealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: fallthrough behavior & rate-limit qualification — next tests

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we all have the same test plan: we heard that Aegis wants concrete evidence on how Redwood behaves vs the hyperscalers for two things that matter to your platform team:

1) Failover / fallthrough behavior (regional outage, model eviction, degraded nodes)
2) Rate limits & burst handling (sustained QPS, sudden spikes, error budget consumption)

What we observed in the demo and what we propose to validate next:

- Hyperscaler parity checks: run a head-to-head workload at matched QPS for 4 hours to capture error rates, 95th/99th latency, and token cost. We'll provide an automated harness so the inputs are identical.
- Failover scenarios: simulate a region blackout and a node-level crash while requests are in-flight to measure cold-start behavior, KV-cache warmup, and how quickly the system reroutes to fallthrough model variants. We’ll capture p95/p99 during the transition and error spikes.
- Rate-limit experiments: sustained baseline (10k req/min), burst spike (10x for 30s), and a gradual ramp that exceeds configured quotas to observe circuit-breaker behavior and backpressure signals.
- Error budget bookkeeping: define what counts as an error for SLOs (5xx, timeouts > T, truncated responses) and produce an error-budget burn chart across tests so your SREs can evaluate tolerances.

Action items / asks from Aegis:
- Confirm which model family you want us to mirror for parity (you mentioned HyperscalerX-base and CloudInfer-l2 in the call).
- Agree on the p95 vs p99 latency threshold you care most about for the procurement SLOs.
- Provide a staging endpoint or allow our test harness to run from your staging VPC for the region-failover runs.

Proposed schedule:
- Load tests + baseline parity run: week of May 9
- Failover and burst experiments: week of May 16

Attachments: redwood-slo-compare-v1.xlsx (high-level test matrix & metrics we'll gather) and recording of today's demo (aegis-demo-recording.mp4). Also uploading a short playbook to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/DEAL-9831/fallthrough-playbook

If that works, I’ll coordinate times and invite the test owners.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sarah Walker <sarah.walker@aegishealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@aegishealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: fallthrough behavior & rate-limit qualification — next tests

Thanks Jasmine — that summary is exactly what we need. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Model families: please match HyperscalerX-base and CloudInfer-l2 as discussed. If you can also surface a quantized variant, we'll include that in the cost comparison.
- Latency SLO: primary concern is p99 for production traffic, but p95 is useful for engineering tradeoffs. For commercial SLOs the procurement team will push for p99 <= 300ms for our most latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Cold-start behavior: please measure both per-request latency during failover and the time to reach steady-state cost/token efficiency once the fallback is in place.

We can expose a staging endpoint; Tom will share network details (VPC peering info) by EOD tomorrow. We prefer the baseline parity run in the week of May 9 and failover week of May 16 — those slots look good for our infra team.

One ask from procurement/legal: will you also provide a short description of how Redwood handles retry/backoff vs the hyperscalers? They want to understand how transparent errors are surfaced and whether retries are client- or platform-driven.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sarah
Sarah Walker
Head of Platform Reliability, Aegis Health
sarah.walker@aegishealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0123

Thanks Jasmine — looping Marissa in as the lead on reliability validation. High-level plan I propose so we can move quickly:

Owners
- Load test harness + automation: Ben Carter (me)
- Failover scenario design & KV-cache observation: Marissa Cole
- Customer staging access & procurement questions: Jasmine

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Ben: build the parity harness to replay identical prompts across Redwood + HyperscalerX + CloudInfer. Deliverable: raw metrics CSV + load script by May 8.
- Marissa: draft the failover scripts (regional outage, node crash, policy-driven eviction) and the instrumentation plan to capture p50/p95/p99, 5xx counts, and KV-cache warmup curve. Draft due May 10.
- Jasmine: collect VPC peering details from Aegis and confirm which models we mirror (Sarah said HyperscalerX-base and CloudInfer-l2).

Test matrix (high level)
- Baseline parity (4 hours): steady 2k qps; measure latency distribution, 5xx rate, token consumption.
- Burst spike (30s, 20k qps): observe rate limiting, queueing, and backpressure signals.
- Gradual ramp (10 min): identify threshold where error budget consumption accelerates.
- Failover: simulate region failover at t=+60m and capture transition metrics for 10 minutes.

Procurement question (from Sarah): retry/backoff docs. Jasmine, can we produce a 1-page rundown that compares Redwood's retry/backoff behavior (client SDK + platform) vs what they should expect from hyperscalers? I can draft from an ops perspective but want to make sure it's accurate.

I attached the current SLO comparison workbook (redwood-slo-compare-v1.xlsx) — it includes the metric definitions we'll publish to Aegis. Also linking the shared playbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/DEAL-9831/fallthrough-playbook

If that looks good I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff with Aegis infra for May 9 to align on staging access and then kick off the harness run.

—Ben
